name: Music
intro: Develop your musical voice through performing, composing and listening. Suggested BGE experiences are flexible ideas for departmental review. Music and Music Technology are different qualifications. Practice examples here support learning and must not be presented as completed assessed compositions. Respect copyright, recording consent and comfortable listening levels; follow school guidance for equipment and practical sessions.

bge.title: Rhythm in everyday life
bge.question: How can a pattern develop?
bge.task: Create a written eight-bar rhythm using a teacher-approved notation system, showing repetition and one change.
bge.extend: Explain how syncopation can challenge the expected beat.

bge.title: Melody and mood
bge.question: Why do melodies feel different?
bge.task: Sketch the contour of a supplied melody and identify a phrase ending.
bge.extend: Compare two interpretations and explain one expressive difference.

bge.title: Music and identity
bge.question: How does music connect communities?
bge.task: Compare two teacher-selected recordings by instrumentation, rhythm and context, avoiding stereotypes.
bge.extend: Find how a contemporary musician adapts a traditional influence.

bge.title: Compose for a scene
bge.question: How does music guide a listener?
bge.task: Plan a short soundtrack for a fictional scene, identifying tempo, texture and intended effect.
bge.extend: Explain how silence could be more effective than adding another sound.

senior.title: Music
senior.explain: Build practical performance, musical creativity and listening knowledge. National 4 adds a performance task.
senior.assessment: Internally assessed units and National 4 added value; pass/fail.

senior.title: National 5 Music
senior.explain: Develop performance on two instruments, or one instrument and voice, alongside composing and listening skills within national requirements.
senior.assessment: Performance, composing assignment and question paper. Teachers confirm repertoire, level and assessment conditions.

senior.title: Higher Music
senior.explain: Increase musical fluency, stylistic understanding and critical listening. Compose and justify choices with more developed musical control.
senior.assessment: Performance, composing assignment and question paper under the current specification.

skills.title: Practise deliberately
skills.explain: Choose a small challenge and use a strategy rather than repeating an entire piece unchanged.
skills.try: Plan a teacher-agreed practice focus such as one rhythmic transition.
skills.check: Can you explain what improved and identify the next precise step?

skills.title: Listen with evidence
skills.explain: Support a concept with an audible feature.
skills.try: Identify an ostinato in a recording and describe its repeated pattern.
skills.check: Distinguish a recurring pattern from merely hearing the same instrument.

skills.title: Develop a motif
skills.explain: Variation changes a musical idea while retaining a recognisable relationship.
skills.try: Propose a rhythmic or pitch variation of a short original motif.
skills.check: Explain what stayed recognisable and what changed.

skills.title: Read notation in context
skills.explain: Connect symbols to sound, timing and expression.
skills.try: Annotate a teacher-provided phrase with pulse and dynamics.
skills.check: Check whether the notation communicates the intended performance consistently.

practice.question: What is the difference between tempo and dynamics? Give a musical example.
practice.hint: One concerns speed; the other concerns loudness.
practice.answer: Tempo describes speed, such as a faster pulse. Dynamics describe loudness, such as a crescendo. A passage can become louder without becoming faster.
practice.extend: Explain how both could change independently during a dramatic scene.

practice.question: A short bass pattern repeats beneath changing melodies. Which concept might describe it, and what evidence supports your answer?
practice.hint: Listen for a persistent repeated pattern.
practice.answer: An ostinato is a repeated musical pattern. Identify the recurring rhythm or pitches in the bass; the instrument alone is not enough evidence.
practice.extend: Explain how changing harmony above the pattern could affect the music.

practice.question: Your composition has four unrelated ideas but no clear shape. Suggest a purposeful improvement.
practice.answer: Develop one motif, contrast it with another section and consider a return such as ABA. This gives the listener relationships to recognise; a structure should serve the intended effect.
practice.extend: Describe one variation that could make the returning A section different.

resources.title: Ableton Learning Music
resources.task: Explore beat, melody or structure in the browser. Explain a choice before changing it.

resources.title: BBC Ten Pieces
resources.task: Choose an orchestral work and identify two audible features. This is a music resource, not Bitesize.

resources.title: Royal Scottish National Orchestra
resources.task: Explore available learning or performance resources and compare orchestral timbres.

resources.title: Scottish Chamber Orchestra
resources.task: Find an available introduction to an instrument or work and connect it to listening vocabulary.

resources.title: Official course and listening guidance
resources.task: Follow your level to current assessment information, past papers and music guidance.

ipad.title: Practice reflection
steps: Record only your own teacher-agreed performance extract.
Identify a timestamp showing one strength and one challenge.
Write a precise next practice step.
ipad.evidence: A focused reflection; do not share classmates’ recordings without consent.

ipad.title: Listening map
steps: Create a timeline of sections, textures and instrumental entries.
ipad.evidence: A map showing musical evidence rather than only mood words.

ipad.title: Composition sketchbook
steps: Create a short original idea in approved software or notation.
Save a version and explain a musical decision.
Revise one feature after teacher feedback.
ipad.evidence: A documented learning process separate from assessed coursework.

careers.title: Performer or music educator
careers.linkToLearning: Practice, interpretation and communication support musical work.
careers.nextStep: Compare college, conservatoire and university entry or audition requirements.

careers.title: Sound engineer
careers.linkToLearning: Listening and understanding musical structure support technical audio work.
careers.nextStep: Explore distinct sound production and music technology college routes.

careers.title: Arts administrator
careers.linkToLearning: Organisation and audience knowledge support events and ensembles.
careers.nextStep: Investigate creative industries courses, entry roles and work experience.

careers.title: Composer or media musician
careers.linkToLearning: Developing musical ideas serves film, games and performance.
careers.nextStep: Build a portfolio and explore composition or commercial music routes.

parentTip: Ask your young person to play or explain one small musical idea and describe their next step. Encourage focused, teacher-agreed practice rather than judging progress by volume or speed.
